newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine guerrilla Gorriaran dismisses his lawyers.
newsitem.headline: Argentine guerrilla Gorriaran dismisses his lawyers.

text.p: Argentine guerrilla Enrique Gorriaran Merlo, on trial for a bloody 1989 attack on the army barracks of La Tablada, got rid of his defence lawyers on Monday, saying he was already a condemned man.

"The guarantees of a proper process are seriously vulnerable, which means I do not want my lawyers to legitimise the trial, which I consider illegitimate, with their presence," Gorriaran told the court.
The trial of Gorriaran, the former Marxist leader of the People's Revolutionary Army (ERP) and the All for the Fatherland Movement (MTP), started last week.
Gorriaran and his former wife, Ana Sivori, face life sentences if found guilty of Argentina's last major guerrilla attack, in which 39 people died, 60 were wounded and three were reported missing.
Sivori decided she did not need her lawyers either. In their dismissal of the proceedings, the two said they did not want to be present in the court until the final verdict.
